name_zh: 克拉斯诺达尔“花束”红茶
processing: Under the old grading system the Bouquet name went to top-scoring tea made from two-leaf flushes, the young upper leaves. As a black tea it then goes through the normal withering, rolling, oxidation and drying.
harvest_season: Young two-leaf flushes; the exact picking dates for this tea are not well documented.
appearance_dry: As with other fine-plucked black teas, expect a dark, neatly twisted small leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typical of the class, a clear reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Typical of young black tea leaf, soft and coppery brown.
taste_profile: Little is recorded about this tea in the cup. Expect what is usual for a young-leaf black tea: a gentle, rounded cup with mild malt and some sweetness.

brewing.notes: These are usual Western-style black tea settings, nothing specific to this tea.

vintage_note: Sold as a current retail product, not by vintage, and years are rarely advertised. The name is now also used on packaged tea, so read the label for the share of local Krasnodar leaf. As with other black teas, drink it within a couple of years.
description:
Bouquet was the top commercial grade in the Soviet tea scale: tea made from two-leaf flushes that scored at least 5.00 points for black tea. Depending on origin it was sold as Bouquet of Georgia, Bouquet of Azerbaijan or Krasnodar tea Bouquet.

Keep the scale in perspective. Fine South Indian and Ceylon teas could score 7 to 8 points, and only very rare teas reached 9 or 10. So Bouquet meant the best of a domestic range, not the top of the world market.

The cup is not well described. Expect a typical young-leaf black tea and brew it like one, and adjust from there.

When buying, do not assume the words guarantee an old-style graded tea or a fully local one. Today's Krasnodar Bouquet is also a packaged shop product, and the 2019 regional standard gives the 100% local top tier a similar but different name: Kuban Bouquet.
history: The name is documented as a grade in the Soviet scoring system. A January 2019 regional association standard for Krasnodar tea then set out tiers by local leaf content, with 100% local leaf for Kuban Bouquet. Little else is documented about when the Krasnodar version first appeared or who first made it.
